body.x: 202 BPM (CEO of BPM, Kim Seung Young) was selected on ‘Local Convergence Sports Industry Base Development Project,’ held by supports from Sports Convergence Industry Support Center of Daegu Technopark, Ministry of Culture, Sports, and Tourism, and Daegu Metropolitan City and took part in ‘CES 2017’ held in Las Vegas in the U.S from January 5th to January 8th to exhibit an indoor exercise equipment, ‘BUFF-UP.’

Sports Convergence Industry Support Center of Daegu Technopark is an organization that vitalizes the regional economy and realizes the government’s policies to develop the local sports industry by generating a great synergy through regional major and strategic industry and convergence of the sports industry, which makes an effort to set up a cluster of the sports industry, activate a facility for advancement of the industry, bring about and spread it, and secure professional capacities and the spread of the specialized regional convergence R&D.

BUFF-UP of 202 BPM is good equipment for doing balance exercises and body weight training together. Through a connection to a smart phone, users can check a schedule, coaching training, and the result of the exercise.

The possibility of BUFF-UP was confirmed in the American market through CES. The CEO of 202 BPM, Kim Seung Young, said, “America is highly interested in exercises, so I wanted to directly experience the reaction of the local markets. Our products have been well received in the United States, and consequently, I would meet a lot of buyers there.”

Meanwhile, the Daegu Technopark and Smart Venture Institute and Smart Drone Technology Center of Kyungpook National University opened ‘CES Daegu Common Facility’ and supported the exhibition operation of 22 domestic enterprises and business meeting with a buyer.

CES (Consumer Technology Show), which is the world’s largest IT consumer electronics and consumer technology tradeshow, is a good opportunity to figure out the flow of the global electronic industry at a glance and is held on every January by CTA (Consumer Technology Association).

Aving News Korea, which have reported issues of CES, MWC, and IFA as the world’ three major technology exhibitions the most for the last 10 years, will send a special group of reporters to CES, report main issues of the markets, and introduce Korean enterprises all over the world this year.
